title: Vanishing of H_1 and freeness of the differentials at a prime give a smooth principal localization
statement: Let $A\to C$ be a homomorphism of commutative rings making $C$ a finitely presented $A$-algebra, and let $\mathfrak q\subset C$ be a prime ideal such that the localization at $\mathfrak q$ of the $C$-module $H_1(L_{C/A})$ [def-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map] vanishes, $H_1(L_{C/A})_{\mathfrak q}=0$, and the localization $(\Omega_{C/A})_{\mathfrak q}$ of the module of Kähler differentials [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials] is a finite free $C_{\mathfrak q}$-module. Then there is $g\in C\setminus\mathfrak q$ such that the ring map $A\to C\to C_g$ is smooth [def-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map] ($C_g$ the localization of $C$ at $\{1,g,g^2,\dots\}$); that is, $A\to C$ is smooth at $\mathfrak q$ in the sense of Algebra, Definition 00TB.
